title: Kernel budgeting and segment reservoir for latency islands in paged KV
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Problem: Some traffic patterns produce 'latency islands'—short tails of requests whose prefill/kv residency costs spike decode latency due to small scattered fragments, unhelpful kernel choices, and contention between prefill and decode waves. Existing slab/eviction heuristics reduce long-term fragmentation but don't prevent short-lived bursts where aggressive kernel choices (large-vector kernels, heavy microfusion) for single decodes steal cycles and cause downstream stalls.

Proposal: Implement two coordinated mechanisms: (1) Kernel budgeting: a runtime controller that enforces a per-decode-wave kernel budget (CPU/GPU cycles proxy) and prefers lower-latency kernel variants for requests that are flagged as latency-sensitive; budgets reset per scheduling epoch and are weighted by tenant priority. (2) Segment reservoir allocator: maintain a small pool of pre-reserved contiguous KV segments (the reservoir) kept compact to satisfy small prefill allocations quickly without fragmenting the main slab. The allocator places short-lived prefill fragments into reservoir segments; long-lived residency goes through normal allocation to avoid starving the reservoir.

Goal: reduce short-tail latency spikes for latency-sensitive requests by limiting costly kernel handoffs and reduce immediate fragmentation from churn-heavy traffic by providing low-latency allocation paths for small prefill needs.
acceptance_criteria: P50 decode latency for 99th-percentile tail workload reduced by >= 20% on benchmark suite 'chat-burst-1000' compared to baseline runtime-1.19
Reservoir hit rate >= 65% for short-lived prefill (<2s) traffic in synthetic churn tests
No regression (>2%) in overall throughput on balanced workload (mixed chat + embeddings)
Unit/integration tests for reservoir allocator and kernel budget controller merged
Design doc and RFC approved by runtime and infra leads
steps: Design RFC: define kernel budget units, epoch length, budget refill policy, tenant weighting
Implement reservoir allocator: compact segment pool, allocation fast path, fallback to normal allocator
Integrate kernel budget controller into scheduler: budget accounting per decode wave, kernel-choice shim
Telemetry: add reservoir hit/miss, budget consumption, kernel variant counts to console metrics
Benchmarks: run chat-burst-1000, multi-tenant churn, and long-tail regression tests
Rollout: staged canary on dedicated pool -> broad rollout with rollback guard
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: RFC drafted and posted to Confluence, initial review from runtime team requested (link below).
2025-02-22: Prototype reservoir allocator implemented in allocator.v2 module; microbenchmarks show 3-4x faster small-allocation path but ~1.5% memory overhead when reservoir sized at 2% of pool.
2025-02-26: Kernel budget shim implemented as scheduler extension. Controlled experiments show reduction in expensive kernel variants by 42% for flagged requests.

2025-03-03: End-to-end integration test failures observed under extreme churn: reservoir exhaustion leads to fallback thrash—added soft admission control and LRU draining hook. Planning follow-up iteration.
2025-03-04: Updated allocator to drain least-recently-used reservoir segments asynchronously; added metrics for reservoir queue length and soft-throttle events.
decisions: Use time-based epochs (100ms) for budget refill instead of token-count refill to simplify cross-model accounting.
Reservoir size default = 2% of pool memory; made configurable per-dedicated-pool via runtime config.
Flagging latency-sensitive requests at ingress (API) rather than inferring from sequence length; SDKs will add header 'X-Redwood-Latency: high' for clients.
Prefer conservative kernel variants by default for flagged requests; provide opt-in override for high-throughput tenants.
review_feedback: PM (Sophie Nguyen): prioritize no regressions on throughput; suggested canary traffic split 5% then 25%.
Infra (Diego Ramos): raised concern about reservoir persistence across pod restarts; suggested durable reservation metadata for graceful rebuild.
Performance (Lena Ortiz): asked for microbench harness to capture kernel-switch cost; shared prototype harness (github link).
Security (TBD): no immediate concerns but requested that kernel-choice telemetry avoid logging raw prompt content.
risks: Reservoir introduces modest memory overhead; if mis-sized it could reduce effective capacity for long-lived workloads.
Incorrect budget tuning may throttle legitimate high-throughput requests causing customer complaints.
Complexity of coordinating allocator + scheduler increases test surface (race conditions during reservoir drain).
testing_plan: Unit tests: allocator invariants, reservoir allocate/free/fallback paths
Integration: end-to-end decode with reservoir under synthetic churn (varying short/long residency ratios)
Perf bench: chat-burst-1000, steady-state throughput, mixed-tenant fairness tests
Canary rollout: 5% dedicated pool -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback triggers on tail latency or error-rate regressions
next_steps: Address reservoir persistence feedback from infra (expected by 2025-03-07)
Tune epoch length and budget units with perf team; run parameter sweep for budget policies (2025-03-08 to 2025-03-12)
Prepare PR for allocator and scheduler changes; link and tests attached
Schedule design review with runtime and infra leads (invite sent)
